`Specs/Resolution.lean` keeps the source vault, a destination vault and the entry list in one state (`TwoChainLedger`). It adds two steps.

- `deliver i wd`: B2's destination `bridgeMint` of entry `i`'s data, called by the router (`twoChainDeliveryCall`).
- `refund i wr`: B2's source `bridgeRecoverFailedTransfer` of the same data, as `recoverAtomicCall` makes it (`twoChainRefundCall`, which is B2's `recoveryCall`).

- A preparation trace (`AssetBridgePreparation.Reach`: vault preparations and ordinary token transfers) runs from a ledger `s` to `t`; `s`'s vault is `WellFormed` and nothing is pending.
- `obs` is a nonempty sub-multiset (`List.Subperm`) of `t.pending`.

Conclusions:
- `claimRefund` on the Revertable leg returns `(Reverted, w')`, and the loop counts `calls.length` calls (`recovered = callsLen`).
- The router maps, registry, pause flag and every other token's ledger are unchanged.
- On the tracked token the config is unchanged. Each account `u` gains exactly `pendingAmountFor u obs`, and supply rises by exactly `pendingAmount obs`. The token stays `WellFormed`.
- For every `rest` with `obs ++ rest ~ t.pending`, new supply + `pendingAmount rest` = `s`'s supply. So refunding the whole pending list restores the pre-trace supply.

No headroom premise: trace conservation supplies it. No hash premise.

No contradiction with the code. Two observations, neither of them exploitable.

(1) Zero commit value: a defense-in-depth gap.
- IndexedMerkleTree.verifyInclusion (common/libraries/IndexedMerkleTree.sol:133-145) does not reject _value == 0. insert does (:69-71), and so does verifyNonInclusion (:160-162).
- AtomicInteropProof.verifyInclusion (atomic-interop/libraries/AtomicInteropProof.sol:113-139) and requireFlowFinalized (atomic-interop/AtomicFlowManager.sol:127-128) pass the commit value through without a nonzero check.
- Every initialized tree holds a value-0 sentinel at index 0: setup writes {0,0,0} (:42-51), and insert keeps a low leaf's value (:96-100).
- So a leg whose commitValue were 0 would verify as finalized against every chain's tree, using the sentinel's own leaf and path. In the model: SharedCommitmentZeroLetsUnappendedLegExecute.
- This needs a keccak preimage of 0: commitValue = uint256(keccak256(abi.encode(TAG, flowId, bundleHash))) (:100-102). A `_value != 0` check in verifyInclusion would remove the exception.

(2) The chain-binding NatSpec holds only up to named exceptions. The claims are at AtomicInteropProof.sol:107-110 ("a leg's commit value can only be inserted into its own source chain's tree, and the membership check below can only pass against that chain"), AtomicFlowManager.sol:117-119 ("membership already self-binds via the chain-specific commitValue") and atomic-interop/README.md:49-50. In the model they hold only up to:
- a keccak collision between the presented leg's preimage and that of a leg appended on that chain (SharedCommitmentClashLetsUnappendedLegExecute: a never-appended leg executes);
- a zero commit value.
The chain-specific half rests on bundleHash embedding block.chainid (interop/InteropCenter.sol:644), which is not modelled (S4). In the model one (flowId, bundleHash) can be appended on two chains (SharedCommitmentSameLegTwoChainsWitness), and then only ProofSourceChainMismatch (AtomicFlowManager.sol:124-126) binds the chain on the inclusion side. So the "defense-in-depth" label is accurate given keccak collision resistance on bundle-hash preimages.

- This is consistent with the stated threat model ("chains are not malicious", InteropHandlerBase.sol:298-301) and with the existing AtomicSourceBinding note.

3. Observation: the binding rests on InteropCenter.sol:644 (hashing with `block.chainid`), not on :500 (`sourceChainId: block.chainid`).
- The handler hashes with the decoded field, so equal preimages force that field to equal the center's `block.chainid`. The proof of `AtomicSourceBoundOrBreak` never uses `FormedBy.source`.
- :500 matters for liveness, not for this safety property: a mismatched field would only make the committed leg unexecutable.

prove.item: A5. Operational projection for InteropAtomicity's fixed history

headlines.meaning: For every node hash h, padding z0, leaf hash hl, commit value cv and flow hash fh, and every run OpSteps h z0 hl cv fh opGenesis Y log clog of the operational model, the history the end state determines (Y.history: the END snapshot and settlement time of every settled batch, the live tree at time Y.now for later batches, height fmHeight of the leaf count) satisfies Contracts.Atomicity.Wf and HeightsFromSource. The operational model is one global interleaving of every chain's append (manager guard plus the tree's full insert flow), authorizeRefund (one leg per step, against a recorded root), claimRefund, initL2, every destination's executeAtomicBundle, and the settlement layer's endBatch, in-order settle at a non-decreasing clock, tick and recordRoot; a call may cite only settled batches. No hash premise.
headlines.witness: OpHonestRunWitness (a run using every step kind, with an execution and a refund authorization in the log); OpLivenessWitness

headlines.meaning: On every run from opGenesis, every recorded root R satisfies AggregatesBefore Y.history R: every batch whose time is strictly before R.created has index at most R.upTo c. No settlement-layer premise: it follows from the steps. Companion IsLastOnTimeDerivedBefore: on any fixed history, AggregatesBefore S R and EndBranchVerified S R c D N give IsLastOnTime S c D N, so the strict form is all the END branch needs. Countermodel OpRootMayMissSameTimeBatch: the non-strict Contracts.Timeout.Aggregates can fail for a recorded root (root recorded at time 0, then chain 0's batch 1 settles at time 0).
headlines.witness: OpHonestRunWitness (its roots even meet non-strict Aggregates); OpRootMayMissSameTimeBatch (strict holds, non-strict fails); OpPaddingRefundLocatesAbsenceBreak exhibits an EndBranchVerified call against a recorded root

headlines.meaning: Every run from opGenesis to Y has its authorizations (authCalls clog) form a Contracts.Refund.ReachLog run from emptyManagers to Y.chains.mgrs over the fixed history Y.history. Companions: OpRunEmbedsInSysSteps (the per-chain steps are a Contracts.AppendPath.SysSteps run from genesisAll to Y.chains over Y.history, with the same append log), OpRunEmbedsInRunLog (manager steps and checked calls are a Contracts.FlowBinding.RunLog run), OpPrefixEmbedsInLaterHistory (a prefix's calls are valid against every later state's history), OpRunSettledHistoryIsFinal (settled batches keep tree, time and height; recorded roots stay), OpLoggedEvidenceIsSettled (every logged call cites settled batches).
headlines.witness: OpHonestRunWitness (nonempty logs, split into two nonempty segments)

headlines.meaning: For every run from opGenesis and every execution e in its checked-call log: the executed leg's obligation is not Refunded in Y's managers, or an authorization in the run's own log that marked it carries a RefundBreak (FlowIdClash with e.flow, or an InclusionBreak on e's proof for the call's missing leg, or an AbsenceBreak on the call's absence proof). No Wf, Aggregates or hash premise. Also transferred the same way: OpOneExecutionFreezesTheFlowOrBreak, OpRefundImpliesOwnFlowTimeoutOrLoggedClash, OpExecutedImpliesAllFinalizableOrBreak, OpSiblingFinalizableNowOrBreak, OpNoneOrAllOrBreakPinned (under DataAvailable), OpLoggedExecutionExcludesLoggedRefundOrBreak, OpExecutedImpliesRealFlowFinalizableOrLoggedClash, OpSystemOncePerLeg, OpRefundedWasAppendedOnce.
headlines.witness: OpHonestRunWitness (break false, not refunded); OpPaddingRefundLocatesAbsenceBreak (the RefundBreak fires and is the absence proof's paddingHit, operationally)

headlines.meaning: New, only possible operationally. For every run from opGenesis, every logged execution e and every leg l of e.flow: the obligation (e.flow.flowId, l.bundleHash, l.chain) was appended on l.chain and is Committed there at the end state (escrowed, never refunded); or its commit value has a CommitClash with an obligation appended on l.chain (pinned to the run's log); or its commit value is 0; or e's inclusion proof for l carries an InclusionBreak; or a RefundBreak on a logged authorization that marked it. Companion OpExecutedLegWasAppendedOrBreak (appended and not Unset, or clash, or zero value, or inclusion break). No hash premise.
headlines.witness: OpHonestRunWitness (first disjunct holds, every other disjunct false); countermodel FixedHistoryAdmitsUnescrowedExecution (over a fixed history a leg executes with no manager ever committing it, nonzero value and no break, so the result cannot be stated there)

headlines.meaning: Liveness as enabledness. For every run from opGenesis to Y, every flow F that passes _checkFlowId (FlowIdChecked fh F) with nonzero commit values (FlowWf cv F), and every recorded root R with F.deadline < R.created: either every leg of F can be executed now (a one-step execute continuation exists, OpFinalizedFlowIsExecutable), or some leg missing of F makes every Committed leg of F refundable now against R (a one-step authorize continuation exists, on the BEGIN branch at the first late batch inside R or on the END branch at R's last batch, OpTimedOutLegIsRefundable, which proves the source's COMPLETENESS paragraph AtomicInteropProof.sol:89-94 including halted chains). OpOnTimeBatchesFinalAfterRoot: after such a root, every batch that later settles is late, so the on-time settled batches never change. The exhibited evidence is the honest proof (presenting it needs PROTO-DA); no fairness or delivery is claimed.
headlines.witness: OpLivenessWitness (one reachable state with a post-deadline root, subsetFlow 0 1 on the executable side and mixedFlow 1 1 2 on the refundable side, plus a nonempty continuation)

headlines.meaning: For a run from opGenesis to X, any authorization a in its log, and any continuation to Y: at every batch of Y's history whose time is at most a.flow.deadline, the missing leg's commit value is not a key of its chain's tree, or a's absence proof carries an AbsenceBreak on X's history (fixed at call time). Companion OpRefundedLegMissedDeadlineOrBreak (same at the run's own end state). The Aggregates premise of the fixed-history TimeoutMeansMissedDeadlineOrBreak is discharged by the strict form.

prove.sourceFindings:
No contradiction between code and NatSpec found. Observations, none a practical defect:
(1) common/libraries/IndexedMerkleTree.sol:133-145: verifyInclusion does not reject value 0 (insert and verifyNonInclusion do, via IMTValueZero), and every tree holds the {0,0,0} sentinel at index 0. A leg whose commitValue is 0 would therefore pass requireFlowFinalized (AtomicFlowManager.sol:127-128) on every chain without any append. Only keccak excludes this: it needs a preimage of 0 for abi.encode(ATOMIC_COMMIT_LEAF_TAG, flowId, bundleHash) (AtomicInteropProof.sol:100-102). The escrow results keep it as a pinned disjunct (legValue cv F l = 0).
(2) The fixed-history premise Aggregates (PROTO-AGGREGATES) is stronger than the source's own soundness argument needs. That argument is "any batch aggregated after it has t' >= T > deadline", AtomicInteropProof.sol:75-76. The strict form suffices, and it holds for every root the modelled settlement layer records, even mid-block. The non-strict form fails for a root taken before a settlement at the same timestamp (OpRootMayMissSameTimeBatch). In the deployed system only end-of-block roots survive the import double check (MessageRootBase.sol:71-79) and L1 timestamps strictly increase, so the non-strict form would also hold there. Safety does not depend on either fact.
(3) Model note, inherited from Contracts.Refund and Contracts.AppendPath: authorizeRefund marks every Committed leg in the manager of the chain running the call (AtomicFlowManager.sol:155-161). The model marks one leg per step on the leg's declared chain. The two agree because bundleHash embeds block.chainid (InteropCenter.sol:644); see backlog S4.
(4) The END-branch refund liveness for a halted chain (OpTimedOutLegIsRefundable) uses the genesis batch with time 0. That is the README's timeout precondition 1 (atomic-interop/README.md:77-93; MessageRootBase.sol:364-387).
